## Purpose
`SpecRow`/`SessionRow` (`lib/dashboard.ts`) and `ArtifactDriftRow`/`ProjectDetectionRow` (`hooks/useArtifactDrift.ts`, `hooks/useProjectDetections.ts`) are the two flavours of "row": a backend-projected list item mirroring a Rust wire shape one-to-one, and a hook-local wrapper row that pairs a fan-out query's per-item loading/error/data state with the item's own identity. Both exist so a list-rendering component can `.map()` over a flat, self-describing array instead of re-deriving loading state per index.

## Convention
Folder: apps/dashboard/src/hooks/**, apps/dashboard/src/lib/** · Extension: .ts · Files of this role in this subproject: 4
`lib`-side rows (`SpecRow`, `SessionRow`) are plain `export interface XRow { ... }` mirroring backend field names verbatim (snake_case), with JSDoc on any field whose meaning isn't obvious from its name (parent/child grouping, sentinel values, provenance). `hooks`-side rows (`ArtifactDriftRow`, `ProjectDetectionRow`) follow one fixed shape instead: the item's identity field (`path`/`project`), the fetched payload as `T | undefined`, `isLoading: boolean`, and `error: unknown` — always these same four kinds of field, always built by zipping a `useQueries` result array back onto the source array by index/path, never returned as the raw TanStack result.

## How to apply
A row projected straight from a backend command belongs next to its fetch wrapper in `lib/*.ts`, named `<Domain>Row`, fields verbatim snake_case. A row that wraps a per-item `useQueries` fan-out belongs in the owning hook's file in `hooks/*.ts`, named `<Domain>Row`, with exactly the `{ identity, data: T | undefined, isLoading, error }` shape shown by `ArtifactDriftRow`/`ProjectDetectionRow` — do not invent additional derived fields on this wrapper row; derive those in the consuming component instead.
